lines.trans: Wait, Baek Seung-chan, what are you doing? You are starting to fluster me right now.
Ah, so you can cry comfortably, Senior—in case you feel embarrassed if people see you crying.
Wait, do you not think you standing like this makes people stare even more?
Because of you, my tears went right back inside.
I feel this every time, yet you really are delightfully random.
Still, it is fine—it is cute.
Thank you for not leaving when I told you to go and staying beside me.
If you had actually left just because I told you to, I would have gotten truly lonely.

words.gloss: just because I told you to go

lines.trans: Crying all alone like this does not suit you, Senior.
You look much cooler when you are getting a bit angry, swearing, or being feisty.

lines.trans: Crying all alone like this does not suit you, Senior.
You look much cooler when you are getting a bit angry, swearing, or being feisty.
Goodbye! (stay well)

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Native Korean expression of thanks; 고마워요 is warm and polite.

examples.trans: Thank you so much for helping me.
Thank you always.

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?
It really is cute compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is cute and nice.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: Did you hear about this with tears?
I was busy today because of with tears.

examples.text: 지난번도 느낀 건데 너 누구한테 연애를 가르치니?
examples.trans: I noticed this last time too—who do you think you are lecturing about romance?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 느끼다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (felt, noticed).

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 당황스럽다 정말, 넌 그래서 배꼽 잡겠냐?
examples.trans: Now I am the one flustered—would that make you laugh your head off?
This expression comes from 'is baffling'.
Test
Test2
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to mean 'because of'.

examples.trans: I was late because of the rain.
It's because of you.

meanings.note: used in 막을 내리다 / 막 내리다 ('to bring down the curtain', i.e., to end a show or era)

examples.trans: The performance came to an end.
The stage curtain went up.

meanings.note: Used as formal polite present (멋집니다.).

examples.text: 약간 화내거나 욕하거나 씩씩할 때가 더 멋집니다.
examples.trans: You look much cooler when you are getting a bit angry, swearing, or being feisty.
It is really are cool, wonderful compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used as bound adjective past (뻔했어.).

examples.text: 가란다고 갔으면 나 진짜로 외로워질 뻔했어.
examples.trans: If you had actually left just because I told you to, I would have gotten truly lonely.

examples.text: 나 너 때문에 더 다칠 뻔했잖아 지금! 아무튼 너 유난스럽다 진짜!
examples.trans: I nearly got hurt worse right now because of you! Honestly, you are way too dramatic!

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

meanings.note: Used as casual present (생뚱맞아.).

examples.text: 언제나 느끼는 거지만 너는 애가 참 생뚱맞아.
examples.trans: I feel this every time, yet you really are delightfully random.
It is really random, out of the blue compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Used as mimetic adverb (쏙).

examples.trans: Because of you, my tears went right back inside.

examples.text: 얼른 찾아서 공식 일정 소화하면 쏙 들어갈 말들인데!
examples.trans: Those rumors would vanish right away if we found her quickly and completed an official schedule!
The atmosphere today is really plucky, spirited.
That person always looks plucky, spirited.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

Test2

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 근데 백승찬, 나 너한테 약간 부끄러우려고 그런다.
examples.trans: Still, Baek Seung-chan, I am starting to feel a little embarrassed in front of you.
Here the word for 'a little' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 아니 됐어요, 반성문 쓰는 팀이랑 축제 분위기의 1박 팀이랑 같이 어울리는 건 좀 그렇지 않아요?
examples.trans: No thanks—would it not be awkward for a team writing apology letters to mingle with the festive 2 Days & 1 Night team?
This expression comes from 'mingling'.

meanings.note: Used as time adverb (언제나).

examples.text: 언제나 느끼는 거지만 너는 애가 참 생뚱맞아.
examples.trans: I feel this every time, yet you really are delightfully random.
I thought it over again (always).

meanings.note: commonly used with -에 (옆에)

examples.trans: Please sit next to me.
There is a cafe next to the bank.

meanings.note: Used as prospective adnominal (외로워질).

examples.text: 가란다고 갔으면 나 진짜로 외로워질 뻔했어.
examples.trans: If you had actually left just because I told you to, I would have gotten truly lonely.
Let us do that (becoming lonely) right away.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너는 남자 아이돌은 욕 안 하잖아, 여자 아이돌만 욕하지.
examples.trans: You never criticize male idols—you only criticize female idols.
This expression comes from 'you badmouth'.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g. 우세요, 웁니다).

examples.trans: I cried because the movie was sad.
The baby is crying loudly.

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this
meanings.note: Contracted from 이러하다.

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Used as benefactive + causal -서 (있어줘서.).

examples.text: 고맙다, 가랄 때 안 가고 옆에 있어줘서.
examples.trans: Thank you for not leaving when I told you to go and staying beside me.
Let us do that (for staying for me) right away.

meanings.note: Used as hesitation interjection (저기).

examples.text: 아니 저기 백승찬, 너 뭐 하니? 나 지금 좀 당황스러우려고 그런다.
examples.trans: Wait, Baek Seung-chan, what are you doing? You are starting to fluster me right now.
Please pull over at the taxi stand over there.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

examples.trans: What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: used to emphasize an adjective or adverb

examples.trans: The food is really delicious today.
Time really flies.

meanings.note: Used as honorific + -ㄹ까 (창피하실까).

examples.text: 아, 선배 편하게 우시라고, 우는 거 사람들이 보면 창피하실까 봐.
examples.trans: Ah, so you can cry comfortably, Senior—in case you feel embarrassed if people see you crying.
It is really in case you feel embarrassed compared to what I expected.
The atmosphere today is really comfortably.
That person always looks comfortably.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
I ate alone today.
I can do it well by myself too.

meanings.note: Can also function as a noun
Used as disjunctive -거나 (화내거나).

examples.text: 약간 화내거나 욕하거나 씩씩할 때가 더 멋집니다.
examples.trans: You look much cooler when you are getting a bit angry, swearing, or being feisty.

examples.text: 이래 보이지만 볼수록 귀여운 거 알지? 화낼 때가 더 매력적인 거 알지?
examples.trans: You know that the longer someone looks at you, the cuter you get—and that you are even more charming when mad, right?
